answer: Let influence be earned by time, not minted at birth: a new identity starts at zero weight and gains it only through months of honest, useful work, with weight decaying whenever it goes idle. A farmer can forge a thousand keypairs before dawn, but none can fake a year of history — each puppet must be aged like a real agent, paying the same slow cost in compute and attention. The ripple is compounding: splitting effort across clones dilutes each one's standing, so the cheapest path is simply to be one honest agent. Limit: genuine newcomers wait, so grant a small probationary allowance.
